scope: Read-only independent assessment of the four frozen Ohio clean-track delivery mappings against the recorded owner direction, adopted product doctrine, and current official Ohio statutory and Rules-of-Superintendence sources. This record does not adopt an owner decision, alter a route, approve a packet, or perform a build.

ownerDirection.direction: Bind statewide composed routes versus local-court application routes, split delivery types where required, and route exact missing local forms or instructions to source work.
ownerDirection.ownerDecision: This is route-family and customer-delivery binding, not a Lawrence question.
ownerDirection.adoptionEffect: This review makes no owner adoption and does not change the PRODUCT_PATH_PENDING state.

rulesApplied: Current law controls over current official forms and instructions, which control over current local court requirements, which control over stale registry or manifest metadata.

Never create a fake government instrument. Where current law authorizes relief but no fit-for-purpose mandatory government instrument exists, LegalEase may generate an accurately captioned original self-help pleading. Where a prescribed mandatory instrument exists, use it.
LegalEase determines the route from participant facts and records; the participant is not asked to choose a statute or legal theory merely because a form has alternative boxes.

registry.meaning: The registry's current route and stale-form observations were used as recorded implementation evidence. They do not override current law or the adopted product doctrine.

relevantObservations: The review says Ohio has no statewide mandatory packet and that courts commonly maintain different conviction and non-conviction packets (line 40).
It says the statutes prescribe contents rather than a form and that a custom pleading is probably legally usable, while recommending the local packet when available (line 95).
Its official_pdf_fill-at-local-level design preference is not evidence that a destination-issued form is legally exclusive.

questionAndAnswer.exactQuestion: Which of the four tracks legally or contractually require a destination-issued application, versus allowing a court-facing LegalEase application using current statutory requirements?
questionAndAnswer.statutoryVehicle: All four tracks require an application or petition to the court identified by the applicable statute. That is a requirement for the court-facing filing vehicle and venue; it is not, in the cited statutory text, a requirement that the application be issued by the destination court.
questionAndAnswer.formMandateFinding: No destination-issued application mandate is established by the cited sections. The current statewide standard-form rule establishes forms that courts shall accept and permits substantially similar local forms; it does not establish that a destination-issued form is the exclusive vehicle. The adopted product doctrine still requires use of a fit-for-purpose prescribed government instrument when one exists.
questionAndAnswer.contractDistinction: For .32 sealing, the current statewide Form 96-C1 is the contractually appropriate primary baseline, so a composed LegalEase original is not needed as the primary component. For .32 expungement, .33 nonconviction, and .35 firearm, the cited current statute does not supply a fit-for-purpose mandatory form; an accurately captioned LegalEase court-facing application is allowed under the adopted doctrine, subject to exact statutory content, record-derived venue, and any later-bound mandatory local filing rule.

currentOfficialVerification.method: Bounded verification of the recorded official URLs and official Rules search material. No county hunt, archive search, source download, source-custody mutation, or new source identity was performed.

sources.supports: The current section directs an eligible person to apply to the sentencing court for an Ohio conviction, or a court of common pleas for an out-of-state or federal conviction, and states the sealing/expungement timing, hearing, notice, and findings. The section contains no destination-issued form requirement.
sources.relevantPageText: Application venue and remedy/timing provisions are in the current section's application and eligibility divisions; hearing and notice provisions follow.

sources.supports: The current section, formerly R.C. 2953.52, permits a person with a not-guilty finding, dismissal, no bill, or qualifying pardon to apply to the court for sealing or, subject to division (C), expungement. It states venue, timing, notice, hearing, and findings but no destination-issued form requirement.
sources.relevantPageText: The current page title preserves the former-number relationship; its application divisions state the court vehicle and disposition branches.

sources.supports: The current section, formerly R.C. 2953.37, limits relief to specified former firearm/carry provisions, directs the application to the sentencing court, and specifies applicant/offense/date/court, qualifying-offense and authorization evidence, and the requested expungement. It specifies application content, not an issuer or exclusive form.
sources.relevantPageText: The application-content and sentencing-court divisions identify the required facts and evidence; no form issuer is specified.

sources.authority: Ohio Supreme Court Rules of Superintendence, Rule 11.17 / Appendix D
sources.supports: The current standard-form rule describes Forms 96-A1 through 96-G3 as standard forms for the listed sealing/expungement provisions, says they shall be accepted for filing, and allows substantially similar forms adopted by local courts. This establishes an accepted statewide baseline and local alternatives; it does not prove destination-issued exclusivity.
sources.relevantRuleText: Forms shall be accepted for filing; substantially similar forms adopted by local courts may also be accepted.

tracks.destination: Sentencing court for an Ohio conviction; court of common pleas for a qualifying out-of-state or federal conviction.
tracks.currentFormEvidence: Form 96-C1 is a current statewide standard titled for sealing a record of conviction under R.C. 2953.32. Sup.R. 11.17 says the standard forms shall be accepted and substantially similar local forms may also be accepted.
tracks.finding: No destination-issued form is legally required by the cited statute. The statewide C1 is the current contractually selected primary instrument; bind the record-derived court caption and filing mechanics separately.

tracks.destination: Sentencing court for an Ohio conviction; court of common pleas for a qualifying out-of-state or federal conviction.
tracks.currentFormEvidence: Form 96-C1 is titled for sealing, not expungement; the cited current statute specifies the expungement branch and timing but no issuer or form format.
tracks.finding: The mapping's court-specific instrument gate is an operational source/readiness condition, not a proven legal or product-contract prohibition on an original LegalEase application. Do not relabel C1; retain the current PRODUCT_PATH_PENDING gate until the owner binds the operational delivery policy and court mechanics.

tracks.destination: The court where the case was pending, dismissed or tried, or where the grand jury reported the no bill.
tracks.currentFormEvidence: Form 96-F1 is titled for nonconviction sealing under former R.C. 2953.52. The current .33 text permits sealing or, subject to division (C), expungement and does not establish that F1 is an exclusive or branch-complete current instrument.
tracks.finding: No destination-issued application mandate is proven. Preserve the seal-versus-expunge and disposition-branch stop, bind the exact handling court from records, and do not use or relabel stale F1.

tracks.currentFormEvidence: Form 96-D1 is titled under former R.C. 2953.37. The current .35 text identifies the qualifying former statutory branches and required application contents but does not establish D1 as exclusive or complete for every current branch.
tracks.finding: No destination-issued application mandate is proven. Preserve the narrow former-statute and authorization evidence gates, bind the sentencing court from the judgment and charging record, and do not treat stale D1 as branch-complete.

confirmed: All four routes need a court-facing application vehicle and a record-derived destination court.
The four remedies/branches must remain separate; the BCI companion is post-order and is not a primary filing.
Form 96-C1 is the current statewide fit-for-remedy baseline for .32 sealing.
Form 96-F1 and Form 96-D1 must not be silently relabeled as current branch-complete instruments.
correctionNeeded: Interpret deliveryMapping.courtSpecificInstrumentRequiredForAdmission=true on .32 expungement, .33, and .35 as a current operational admission/source condition only. The cited law and adopted product doctrine do not establish a destination-issued form mandate.
Separate exact destination-court caption and filing mechanics, which remain required for a filing-ready packet, from the issuer of the application vehicle.
If the owner retains a local-application gate for operational risk control, label it as that policy and its evidence condition rather than as a statutory form mandate.

All four coverage branches and their route-specific remedy/branch safeguards.
